svg.aria-label: The loop one institute ran once becomes a tool any laboratory can run and keep, in two kinds
svg.text: The loop one institute ran once becomes a tool any laboratory can run and keep

g.text: A. What scBaseCount showed
An agent finds and annotates SRA experiments; a fixed
pipeline reprocesses them: 502 million cells, one assay.
Built once by one institute on a cloud platform,
and offered as a blueprint rather than a tool.
B1. A laboratory that already holds the data
A curated table that wants search, browse and
download pages, hosted without a server to keep up.
Today: a framework, templates, a host, and the
student who built the site.
B2. A laboratory that still has to collect
Every public dataset on its tissue, organism or
perturbation, processed with its own tools. Today:
a search, a spreadsheet, a fetcher, a workflow
manager, a cluster account, and a person.
C. DataBaseAgent: two kinds of project, one tool
One local workbench; inspect, build and preview.
Static: publish what you have.
Data + domain SKILL guide Agent-written pages.
Preview, revise and export a self-contained site;
publish through a separately configured provider.
Collecting: collect what you need.
Free-text criteria; any assay; any shell steps; jobs
on the laboratory's own server, outliving the laptop.
Agents act only through validated, recorded
commands; every decision carries a reason and an
author; agents run only when asked.
Locked versions, snapshots, manifests and checksums
keep the repository maintainable after it is built.
Dynamic sites at scale: limitation and future work.
